apiKeys.installer.title: Automatic Codex + Claude Code setup
apiKeys.installer.introduction: Install Codex CLI and Claude Code first. The script below does not install clients or call the API; it only configures the Lumen provider in {configPath} (or {codexHome}) and your shell profile. Enter the key at the hidden prompt in your local terminal. Check the download address and script contents before running it.
apiKeys.installer.posixHelp: Requires Python 3.11+ and an interactive terminal. The key is stored in a user-only file (0600); the profile stores only the configuration that reads that file.
apiKeys.installer.windowsHelp: Run on Windows. The key is encrypted with the current user’s DPAPI and protected by a user-only ACL. Configure each PowerShell edition you use (5.1 and 7).
apiKeys.installer.modelHelp: The installer asks for the Codex and Claude Code model public API IDs and backs up changed configuration. Your existing Codex default model and provider are preserved. Run {command} only if you explicitly chose to change the default model to a Lumen model. Otherwise, specify the model with the {modelOption} command below. Open a new terminal to apply profile settings. Also specify the model with {modelOption} if profile or project settings override it.
apiKeys.installer.unavailable: Automatic setup requires HTTPS Lumen addresses and an HTTPS dashboard. Only local loopback HTTP previews are exempt; use the manual setup below in other environments.
apiKeys.codex.defaultModelHelp: You can run the command below if you chose to change the default model during setup, or the top-level {model} in your user configuration is the public API ID of the Lumen model you want, and profile or project settings do not override it. {modelProvider} alone does not select a model; use {modelOption} above when you have a different default model or a model override.
apiKeys.guide.signIn: Sign in to view Lumen connection information.
apiKeys.codex.title: Codex CLI (Responses)
apiKeys.codex.introduction: First, safely store the ordinary API key you issued and check the public API ID to use in the model selector. The public API address in the configuration below was retrieved from this environment. Do not paste the key into the configuration file or this screen; enter it in the shell you will use. Set {providerHeader} only when the same ID exists across multiple providers.
apiKeys.codex.configHelp: Add only the provider block below to {configPath}. It does not overwrite your existing {model}· {modelProvider} defaults. If a block with the same name already exists, update its contents.
apiKeys.codex.keyPromptHelp: First, run only the single line below in your shell, enter the full issued key directly into the hidden input prompt, and press Enter. Pasting all remaining commands at once may enter the next command instead of the key.
apiKeys.codex.runHelp: Then replace {modelId} below with the public API ID of an active Responses-compatible model from the model selector and run it in the same shell. The CLI options replace the existing default provider for this run only.
apiKeys.codex.tlsHelp: If your browser and curl work but Codex fails to connect over TLS with {requestError}, set {certificateVariable} to a PEM bundle trusted by this device and run it again in the same shell. If the files below do not exist or your distribution differs, use the device’s trusted bundle. Do not disable TLS verification.
apiKeys.claudeCode.title: Claude Code (Anthropic API)
apiKeys.claudeCode.introduction: Prepare the ordinary API key you issued and check the public API ID of an active Anthropic Messages-compatible model in the model selector. First, run only the single line below in your shell, enter the full key directly into the hidden prompt, and press Enter. Pasting the next command at the same time may enter a command instead of the key. Enable the two provider ID and custom header lines only when the same model ID exists across multiple providers.
apiKeys.claudeCode.runHelp: Then replace {modelId} below with the selected public API ID and run it in the same shell. It connects directly to the retrieved Anthropic API origin, and the key is not included in the copied command.
